# Go Defaults

<!-- Generated by npm run docs; edit scripts/README.template.md. -->

**Apply defaults when a value or object property is missing or `undefined`.**

[![Source line coverage](https://img.shields.io/badge/coverage-100%25-brightgreen.svg)](#development)
[![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-100%25-brightgreen.svg)](docs/API.md)

- **Version:** [2.0.0](CHANGELOG.md)
- **Licence:** [MIT](LICENSE.md)

Use [`withDefaults(defaults, ...overrides)`](docs/API.md#withdefaultsdefaults-overrides) to combine defaults and overrides into a new object. Overrides apply from left to right. Missing properties and `undefined` keep earlier values, while defined values such as `null`, `false`, `0` and empty strings take precedence. This follows the same fallback rule as JavaScript default parameters and destructuring defaults. The merge is shallow, so nested objects and arrays keep their original references.

Use [`createDefaultsMerger(options)`](docs/API.md#createdefaultsmergeroptions) to create a reusable merge function with a custom fallback rule, nested merging, or both.

For a single value, use [`defaultIf(value, fallback, predicate?)`](docs/API.md#defaultifvalue-fallback-predicate). By default, it uses the fallback only when the value is `undefined`. Pass a predicate to choose a different condition.

To add defaults to an existing function’s arguments, see [`withDefaultArgs`](https://github.com/fishgoldworks/go-fns/blob/master/docs/API.md#withdefaultargsfn-defaultargs) in [`go-fns`](https://github.com/fishgoldworks/go-fns) 2.0.

No runtime dependencies. TypeScript declarations included.

## Installation

Using npm:

```sh
npm install go-defaults
```

Using Yarn:

```sh
yarn add go-defaults
```

### Runtime support

| Environment | Requirement                                                                           |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CommonJS    | Node.js 8.0.0 or later, including root and function subpaths.                         |
| ES modules  | Node.js 12.17.0+ within 12.x, or Node.js 14.0.0 and newer.                            |
| Browser     | Standalone ES2017 bundles; requires `Reflect.ownKeys`. See [browser usage](#browser). |

- **Polyfills:** The library does not install global polyfills.
- **Browser modules:** The `dist/index.mjs` entry and function `.mjs` entries wrap CommonJS and require a bundler for browser use; use the [browser bundles](#browser) for direct script loading.

## Usage

### ES modules

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
import { withDefaults, createDefaultsMerger, defaultIf } from 'go-defaults';

// Combine object defaults with overrides.
withDefaults({ title: 'Home', visible: true }, { visible: false });  // => { title: 'Home', visible: false }

// Reuse an object merger that falls back for null or undefined.
const merge = createDefaultsMerger({ shouldFallback: value => value == null });
merge({ title: 'Home' }, { title: null });  // => { title: 'Home' }

// Use a fallback when a single value is undefined.
const title = undefined;
defaultIf(title, 'Home');  // => 'Home'
```

### CommonJS

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
const { withDefaults, createDefaultsMerger, defaultIf } = require('go-defaults');

// Combine object defaults with overrides.
withDefaults({ title: 'Home', visible: true }, { visible: false });  // => { title: 'Home', visible: false }

// Reuse an object merger that falls back for null or undefined.
const merge = createDefaultsMerger({ shouldFallback: value => value == null });
merge({ title: 'Home' }, { title: null });  // => { title: 'Home' }

// Use a fallback when a single value is undefined.
const title = undefined;
defaultIf(title, 'Home');  // => 'Home'
```

### Function subpaths

Import a function by subpath when you only need that function.

```javascript
import withDefaults from 'go-defaults/withDefaults';
```

These paths support default and named ES module imports. In CommonJS, `require('go-defaults/withDefaults')` returns the function directly.

Root and subpath imports refer to the same functions. See [TypeScript](#typescript) for module-resolution requirements.

### Browser

Load Go Defaults from jsDelivr or host a bundle yourself:

- [Minified bundle](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/go-defaults@2.0.0/dist/go-defaults.min.js)
- [Readable bundle](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/go-defaults@2.0.0/dist/go-defaults.js)

The bundle exposes `goDefaults`:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/go-defaults@2.0.0/dist/go-defaults.min.js"></script>
<script>
  const { withDefaults, createDefaultsMerger, defaultIf } = goDefaults;

  // Combine object defaults with overrides.
  withDefaults({ title: 'Home', visible: true }, { visible: false });  // => { title: 'Home', visible: false }

  // Reuse an object merger that falls back for null or undefined.
  const merge = createDefaultsMerger({ shouldFallback: value => value == null });
  merge({ title: 'Home' }, { title: null });  // => { title: 'Home' }

  // Use a fallback when a single value is undefined.
  const title = undefined;
  defaultIf(title, 'Home');  // => 'Home'
</script>
```

The bundles are self-contained and also support CommonJS and AMD loaders.

### Combine several override sources

Combine application defaults with saved preferences and page-specific overrides. Put the most specific overrides last. An `undefined` page size keeps the saved preference instead of resetting it to the initial default.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
import { withDefaults } from 'go-defaults';

const defaults = { theme: 'light', pageSize: 20, showHints: true };
const savedPreferences = { theme: 'dark', pageSize: 50 };
const pageOverrides = { pageSize: undefined, showHints: false };

const settings = withDefaults(defaults, savedPreferences, pageOverrides);
settings;   // => { theme: 'dark', pageSize: 50, showHints: false }
```

### Apply defaults to a list of objects

Pass the same defaults to `withDefaults` for each object in the list.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
import { withDefaults } from 'go-defaults';

const defaults = { visible: true };
const pages = [{ title: 'Home' }, { title: 'About', visible: false }];
const completePages = pages.map(page => withDefaults(defaults, page));

completePages;   // => [{ visible: true, title: 'Home' }, { visible: false, title: 'About' }]
```

### Keep defaults for unanswered form fields

If a form sends `null` for unanswered fields, set `shouldFallback` to keep earlier values for both `null` and `undefined`. Other changes, such as switching off email updates, still apply.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
import { createDefaultsMerger } from 'go-defaults';

const mergeForm = createDefaultsMerger({ shouldFallback: value => value === null || value === undefined });
const defaults = { language: 'en', emailUpdates: true };
const submitted = { language: null, emailUpdates: false };

mergeForm(defaults, submitted);  // => { language: 'en', emailUpdates: false }
```

### Merge a nested record

Set `mergeDepth: 1` to merge matching records directly inside the root. Earlier properties in `params` carry forward when the override leaves them out.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
import { createDefaultsMerger } from 'go-defaults';

const merge = createDefaultsMerger({ mergeDepth: 1 });
const defaults = { params: { limit: 10, order: 'name' } };
merge(defaults, { params: { limit: 20 } });  // => { params: { limit: 20, order: 'name' } }
```

### Resolve the default theme

Use `'light'` when the theme setting is `'default'`.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
import { defaultIf } from 'go-defaults';

function theme(mode) {
  return defaultIf(mode, 'light', value => value === 'default');
}

theme('default');  // => 'light'
theme('dark');     // => 'dark'
```

### Use a fallback when volume conversion fails

Use `50` when the volume setting converts to `NaN`.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
import { defaultIf } from 'go-defaults';

function volume(text) {
  return defaultIf(Number(text), 50, Number.isNaN);
}

volume('loud');  // => 50
volume('0');     // => 0
volume('75');    // => 75
```

### Object defaults

| API | Description | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`withDefaults(defaults?, ...overrides)`](docs/API.md#withdefaultsdefaults-overrides) | Performs a shallow merge of defaults and overrides into a new object, preserving earlier values when a property is missing or `undefined`. | **`Object`**<br><br>A new plain object containing the combined properties. Nested objects and arrays retain their original references. |
| [`createDefaultsMerger(options?)`](docs/API.md#createdefaultsmergeroptions) | Creates a reusable function that merges objects with your defaults rules. | **`Function`** — `(defaults?, ...overrides) => Object`<br><br>A reusable function that returns a fresh plain object. |

### Single-value defaults

| API | Description | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`defaultIf(value, fallback, predicate?)`](docs/API.md#defaultifvalue-fallback-predicate) | Returns a fallback if a value meets a condition. | **`any`**<br><br>The fallback when the predicate returns `true`. Otherwise, the supplied value. References are preserved. |

## Behaviour

The object helpers copy only own enumerable string and symbol properties. Inherited and non-enumerable properties are skipped, and each eligible getter is read once. Special keys such as `__proto__` become own data properties without changing the result's prototype; see [property copying](docs/API.md#property-copying) for the complete rules and limits.

The merge creates new objects at the levels it visits. Branches assigned as whole values keep their references. The object helpers do not write to their sources, but getters and proxies can have side effects or throw.

[`withDefaults`](docs/API.md#withdefaultsdefaults-overrides) and functions created by [`createDefaultsMerger`](docs/API.md#createdefaultsmergeroptions) accept objects and skip whole `null` or `undefined` arguments. Primitive and function arguments throw `TypeError`. Property values may be any type, including functions.

Object layers are processed in order. Side effects that occur before an error are not undone.

[`defaultIf`](docs/API.md#defaultifvalue-fallback-predicate) selects one whole value. A defined object is returned by reference, even if some of its properties are missing. It does not inspect properties, invoke functions or await promises. See the [whole-value and object-default examples](docs/API.md#defaultifvalue-fallback-predicate).

Both the value and the fallback are required. Either may explicitly be `undefined`. A custom predicate must return a primitive boolean.

## TypeScript

TypeScript declarations are included; no separate `@types` package is required.

[`defaultIf`](docs/API.md#defaultifvalue-fallback-predicate) infers the selected type with the built-in test. A custom predicate gives a union of the value and fallback types. See [single-value inference](docs/API.md#single-value-inference).

For ordinary objects with known properties, TypeScript infers each result property's type from the defaults and overrides. Dictionaries, arrays, recognised native instances and source lists beyond the inference limit produce unknown-valued properties instead. TypeScript cannot determine property ownership or enumerability; widen custom class instances or unusual objects to `object` when that assumption does not hold. See the [typing examples and limits](docs/API.md#typescript).

With a [custom override rule](docs/API.md#inference-with-a-custom-rule), an earlier value can remain and a property supplied only in overrides can be absent. The inferred result reflects both outcomes.

Consumer declarations support TypeScript 4.5.2 or later. Node16/NodeNext resolution requires TypeScript 4.7.2 or later, and Bundler resolution requires 5.0.2 or later. See [compiler support](docs/API.md#compiler-support) for the tested versions and resolution modes.

Named imports from function subpaths require Node16, NodeNext or Bundler resolution. With legacy `node` resolution, use named root imports or default subpath imports. Default subpath imports need `esModuleInterop` for CommonJS output, or `allowSyntheticDefaultImports` for ES module output.

## Performance

Each object merge visits the input objects' own keys and allocates a new result. At positive depths, later overrides can update a branch already created by the same merge. [`defaultIf`](docs/API.md#defaultifvalue-fallback-predicate) returns an existing value without cloning it.

## Development

Use npm for development. Contributor tools require Node.js 22.16.0 or later, excluding Node.js 23. This requirement is separate from [consumer runtime support](#runtime-support). Contributor checks use TypeScript 6.0.3.

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
npm test
```

Edit `scripts/README.template.md` and `scripts/API.template.md`. `npm run build` regenerates both documents before staging the complete consumer package under `package/`, including browser bundles in `package/dist/`. Use `npm run docs` to regenerate documentation independently.

Run the standard gate on a supported contributor Node version:

```sh
npm run verify
```

`npm run verify` checks lint, formatting, generated documentation, source coverage, declarations, build recovery, package contents and installed consumers. `npm run verify:all` adds Chromium, Firefox and WebKit checks against the same archive, including the browser bundles and README example.

See the [development guide](https://github.com/fishgoldworks/go-defaults/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for browser setup, exact-runtime selection, build recovery and release verification.

The coverage badge measures executable source-line coverage. The documentation badge measures public API reference coverage. Neither badge guarantees correctness for every input.

The development root is private and rejects root packing and publication. Build and install a local package with:

```sh
npm run pack:package
npm run test:package -- --tarball ./artifacts/go-defaults-2.0.0.tgz
npm install ./artifacts/go-defaults-2.0.0.tgz
```
